title: msrp_ua Module
content_markdown:
This module implements an User Agent capable of establishing messaging sessions using the MSRP(RFC 4976) protocol.

Through an internal API and exported script and MI functions, the module allows OpenSIPS to set up MSRP sessions via SIP and exchange messages as an MSRP endpoint.

The module makes use of the _proto\_msrp_ module for the MSRP protocol stack and the _b2b\_entities_ module for the SIP UAC/UAS functionalities.
overview:
This module implements an User Agent capable of establishing messaging sessions using the MSRP(RFC 4976) protocol.

Through an internal API and exported script and MI functions, the module allows OpenSIPS to set up MSRP sessions via SIP and exchange messages as an MSRP endpoint.

The module makes use of the _proto\_msrp_ module for the MSRP protocol stack and the _b2b\_entities_ module for the SIP UAC/UAS functionalities.
how_it_works:
In order to start a SIP call carying MSRP from OpenSIPS you can use the [msrp\_ua\_start\_session](#mi_msrp_ua_start_session "1.6.2.� msrp_ua_start_session") MI function. Alternatively, to answer a SIP session with MSRP you can use the [msrp\_ua\_answer()](#func_msrp_ua_answer "1.5.1.� msrp_ua_answer(content_types)") script function.

When a UAC or UAS session is successfully established(ACK sent/received) the [E\_MSRP\_SESSION\_NEW](#event_E_MSRP_SESSION_NEW "1.7.1.� E_MSRP_SESSION_NEW") event is triggered. After this point, you may receive MSRP messages or Reports, signaled by the [E\_MSRP\_MSG\_RECEIVED](#event_E_MSRP_MSG_RECEIVED "1.7.3.� E_MSRP_MSG_RECEIVED") and [E\_MSRP\_REPORT\_RECEIVED](#event_E_MSRP_REPORT_RECEIVED "1.7.4.� E_MSRP_REPORT_RECEIVED") events.

Note that the _E\_MSRP\_REPORT\_RECEIVED_ event covers both actual MSRP REPORT requests as well as negative MSRP transaction responses and local send timeouts(which should be treated the same as a received timeout transaction response).

You can send MSRP messages to the peer with the [msrp\_ua\_send\_message](#mi_msrp_ua_send_message "1.6.1.� msrp_ua_send_message") MI function.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash table that stores the MSRP session information. It is the 2 logarithmic value of the real size.

exported_parameters.name: cleanup_interval
exported_parameters.description: The interval between full iterations of the sessions table in order to clean up expired MSRP sessions.

exported_parameters.name: max_duration
exported_parameters.description: The maximum duration of a call. If set to 0, there will be no limitation.

exported_parameters.name: my_uri
exported_parameters.description: The MSRP URI of the OpenSIPS endpoint. This URI will be advertised in the SDP offer provided to peers when setting up a session and should match one of the MSRP listeners defined in the script. The _session-id_ part of the URI should be ommited. If the port is not set explicitly, the default value of 2855 wil be assumed

exported_parameters.name: advertised_contact
exported_parameters.description: Contact to be used in the generated SIP requests. For sessions answered by OpenSIPS, if it is not set, it is constructed dynamically from the socket where the initiating request was received. This parameter is mandatory when using the msrp_ua_start_session MI function.

exported_parameters.name: relay_uri
exported_parameters.description: URI of an MSRP relay to use for both accepted and initiated sessions. Credentials for the MSRP client are provided via the _uac_auth_ module by setting the _credential_ module parameter. If not set, no relay will be used.

exported_functions.name: msrp_ua_answer

parameters.name: content_types
parameters.description: content types adevertised in the accept-types SDP attribute. At least one of the content types in this list must match the types offered by the peer in its SDP offer.

exported_functions.description: This functions answers an initial INVITE offering a new MSRP messaging session. After this function is used to initialize the session, the call will be completely handled by the B2B engine.

exported_mi_functions.name: msrp_ua_send_message

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: the MSRP session identifier ("session-id" part of the MSRP URI).

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: MIME content type of this message. If missing, an empty message will be sent.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: actual message body. If missing, an empty message will be sent.

parameters.name: success_report
parameters.description: string indicating whether to request an MSRP Success Report. Possible values are yes or no. If the parameter is missing or is set to "no" the SEND request will not include a Success-Report header.

parameters.name: failure_report
parameters.description: string indicating whether to request an MSRP Failure Report. Possible values are yes, no or partial, as specified in MSRP. If the parameter is missing or is set to "yes" the SEND request will not include a Failure-Report header. Note that if the header field is not present, the receving MSRP endpoint must treat it the same as a Failure-Report header with a value of "yes".

exported_mi_functions.description: Sends a new MSRP message to the peer.

examples.code:
opensips-cli -x mi msrp_ua_send_message \
	session_id=5addd9e7b74fa44fbace68a4fc562293 \
	mime=text/plain body=Hello success_report=yes

exported_mi_functions.name: msrp_ua_start_session

parameters.name: content_types
parameters.description: content types adevertised in the accept-types SDP attribute.

parameters.name: from_uri
parameters.description: From URI to be used in the INVITE.

parameters.name: to_uri
parameters.description: To URI to be used in the INVITE.

parameters.name: ruri
parameters.description: Request URI and destination of the INVITE.

exported_mi_functions.description:
Starts a MSRP session.

The advertised_contact is mandatory if this function is used.

examples.code:
opensips-cli -x mi msrp_ua_start_session \
	text/plain sip:oss@opensips.org \
	sip:alice@opensips.org sip:alice@opensips.org

exported_mi_functions.description: Lists information about ongoing MSRP sessions.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: the MSRP session identifier ("session-id" part of the MSRP URI).

exported_events.name: E_MSRP_SESSION_NEW
exported_events.description: This event is triggered when a new MSRP session is successfully established(ACK sent/received).

parameters.name: from_uri
parameters.description: The URI in the SIP From header of the answered INVITE.

parameters.name: to_uri
parameters.description: The URI in the SIP To header of the answered INVITE.

parameters.name: ruri
parameters.description: The SIP Request URI of the answered INVITE.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The MSRP session identifier ("session-id" part of the MSRP URI).

parameters.name: content_types
parameters.description: The content types offered by the peer in the _accept-types_ SDP attribute.

exported_events.name: E_MSRP_SESSION_END
exported_events.description: This event is triggered when an ongoing MSRP session is terminted (session expires or BYE is received; terminating a session via the _msrp_ua_end_session_ MI function is not included).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The MSRP session identifier ("session-id" part of the MSRP URI).

exported_events.name: E_MSRP_MSG_RECEIVED
exported_events.description: This event is triggered when receiving a new, non-empty MSRP SEND request from the peer.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The MSRP session identifier ("session-id" part of the MSRP URI).

parameters.name: content_type
parameters.description: The content type of this message.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The actual message body.

exported_events.name: E_MSRP_REPORT_RECEIVED
exported_events.description:
This event is triggered when:
* a MSRP REPORT request is received
* a failure transaction response is received
* a local timeout for a SEND request occured.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The MSRP session identifier ("session-id" part of the MSRP URI).

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The value of the Message-ID header field.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The value of the Status header field.

parameters.name: byte_range
parameters.description: The value of the Byte-Range header field.
